newsitem.title: USA: Cinergy, Trigen in energy joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Cinergy, Trigen in energy joint venture.

text.p: Cinergy Corp. and Trigen Energy Corp. said Tuesday they will form a joint venture to provide significantly cheaper energy and reduced capital requirements for large energy users.

Each company will invest up to $100 million in developing joint projects through the 50-50 venture, Trigen-Cinergy Solutions LLC. By borrowing against the $200 million in equity, the company can finance as much as $1 billion in projects, they said.

Trigen-Cinergy will build, own and operate facilities that provide heating, cooling and electricity for industrial plants, office buildings, shopping centres, hospitals, universities and other major energy users. It will also provide energy and asset management services.

Combining the production of thermal and electric energy can cut fuel use by up to 50 percent, cut pollution by 90 percent and save users 10 percent to 20 percent of their energy costs, the companies said.
Construction is already under way on a chilled water system to provide air conditioning for the central business district in Cincinnati. Service is expected to begin in April, they said.

Cincinnati-based Cinergy is the nation's 13th largest investor-owned electric company in terms of owned generating capability, with 1995 revenues of $3.03 billion and assets of $8.2 billion. It serves 1.4 million electric customers and 440,000 gas customers.

Trigen, based in White Plains, N.Y., combines heat and power generation, producing electricity as a by-product, for use in its facilities and for sale to customers. It had assets of $460 million and sales of $200 million in 1995.
Cinergy's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $33.50, and Trigen rose 37.5 cents to $30 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
